THE READING, CONFIRMED. POSIX Popen._communicate (subprocess.py:2062) registers self.stdout with a selector, reads data = os.read(key.fd, 32768) (2135) until b'', then decodes (2153). It never touches the file object's buffer. Windows _communicate (1603) starts _readerthread (1598), which runs buffer.append(fh.read()) (1599) on the file object, so it drains whatever readline left behind. The read-ahead: in text mode self.stdout is a TextIOWrapper over a BufferedReader (1016-1018). readline fills its decoded buffer through textiowrapper_read_chunk (textio.c:1843), which calls buffer.read1(chunk_size), chunk_size 8192 (textio.c:1191, 1905-1911). With nothing buffered, BufferedReader.read1 makes one raw read of up to n bytes (bufferedio.c:1001-1028). So one readline takes every byte the pipe holds at that moment, up to 8192, and keeps whatever follows the first newline inside the TextIOWrapper. communicate's fast path (1186-1189) is skipped, because a timeout is given.

LOSS REPRODUCED (Windows 11, Python 3.14.4). A child writes LOADED and 'PowerFloorRefused 0.0001' and exits. The parent waits, then readline() returns 'LOADED\n', os.read(fileno, 32768) returns b'', and file.read() returns the answer. 3 of 3, rc 0 each time.
